answer: One applicant leases a juniper drying yard on a meadow edge for 120 days, for 150 tokens and a 90 dollar license. Forty juniper shrubs in the yard wear numbered bands, and the keeper weighs the weekly berry harvest as a neighbor signs the tally. A zephyr gauge logs noon wind beside the weight, so a forged harvest clashes with the wind record. A false tally forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 yards freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars, like planting fake trees that still need watering, and each fake yard burns its deposit on inspection.
